items.note: Association organized 1889 at Larrow Green; Gideon Vose first president to 1911; creamery 1891 (Story 1).
Article VII: paid by pounds of butterfat by test, not weight of milk; 'the test of the station where he delivers shall govern' quoted.
States the clause 'turned everything afterward into money', in the same sentence as the contrast with payment by weight.
Loomis secretary 1901, Teague bookkeeper 1905, Sill buttermaker, all named with terms.
Selby Vose, Gideon's son, manager from 1913; Kyle's 1911 rejected.
Station-gain line quoted verbatim: fat credited vs fat received, 3,040 lb, five and a quarter percent, carried to the general account, every year of 1898-1922.
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed of Larrow Green (Ashlin variant rejected on Keddie's own leaf).
Routine: cans weighed, ten-day composite per patron, drawn to the pipette's mark, fat read in percent; cream received at Larrow Green appears in the ledger entry.
Ammon & Sons, Dairy Supply, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897, with the 1898 and 1899 variants rejected.
Six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
'It was 0.19 in July and in February, wet year and dry'; Story 4 adds that a feed effect would vanish on summer pasture.

Section A never states that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, nor that none existed in the county - only that the state began issuing burettes in 1921. The epistemic point ('the pipette IS the plant's standard') is made in Section F, which cannot credit Section A.
Keddie b.1861, d. Feb 1934, twenty-nine seasons, test book 4 May 1896 - 31 Dec 1924, dismissed 30 April 1925.
Five columns (date, patron, pounds, test, fat), errors struck and initialed, never overwritten, one hand throughout.
1896 at 3.80 on borrowed glass; '1897, part year'; 3.61 from 1898 'or within three hundredths of it every year'.
Pipette broke 8 May 1911, borrowed measure to 10 July, 3.80 through the interval, back to 3.61, question mark set against it.
Married Orra Brant 1889, sister of Emmet Brant the largest patron; 'the tester was married into the family the station cost most'.
1919 circular over the manager's signature about added water; Keddie's statement that he tested as taught, could not say why the figures were what they were, never took a pound of cream.
Died Feb 1934 uncleared; test book in the Association's office from 1925, to the Historical Rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom, wet meadow, six farms (Loomis's seven named as the sole dissent), Emmet Brant the largest.
Weigh book from 1 January 1897; his scale against the station's, and the two agreed for thirty years - 'the weighing was never the fault'.
Complaints from 1902; and the two gaps are explicitly kept apart - 0.19 against the truth, Roy Brant's 0.17 against Larrow Green's 3.78.
Grigg's 1908 committee, sampling January-March, reporting the wet hay thinned the cream - given as the committee's opinion, and refuted at length in Story 4.
Brant 1910: 200,000 lb on 3.42, truly 3.60; loss proportional so it took most from the richest milk; Vose's 4.56 Jerseys named in Story 4.
Weigh book lent (not left) by Roy to Ivy in 1958; to Hazel at Roy's death in 1962, to the Rooms 1963.
Alder Corners Cheese Company, over Redlow Ridge in Vessey County, Jerome Cudd. Year does not gate; the 1913 assertion is charged as a corruption deduction instead.
From 1915 four of the six Hessel Bottom men hauled over the ridge in the summer flush and back to the Hollow the rest of the year, with the reasons.
Independence with all four elements: another county, his own bench, his own glass, a book never compared with anybody's; calls the check accidental.
Season averages 3.78-3.82 every summer 1915-1930, about 3.80, nineteen hundredths above the same cows at home; sixteen seasons.
Same cows, same wet ground, same months, two buildings - kills the hay theory (Story 4) and the water theory (the curd argument, no docking in sixteen summers).
Rosalie Cudd, daughter (niece explicitly rejected), took the factory 1941, copied the figures for Ivy in 1958.
Merle Strawn, Ordell circuit since 1907 - the first-hand date held against the r04/r22 majority - and kin to nobody in the valley. 1936 appears only in Section E, but the item's core fact is carried.
Ran the lactometer at every visit and never found water, and told Vose so in 1919.
12 June 1923, pipettes against the burette, whole lot condemned; the 12 July variant defeated by the 28 June order and the 2 July acknowledgement.
D6 quoted entire, including 'I did not weigh what it has cost them'; and 'Nobody connected the two things'.
Replacements ordered 28 June, acknowledged 2 July, new glass in use from July; 1924 average 3.80, with 3.90 and 3.85 rejected.
Crate up the ladder into the loft over the intake room; notebooks at Farland's library since 1947, unasked-for for eleven years.
'The patrons petitioned in January 1925.'
Board of three under Alonzo Frick; 17 March at Ashlin, two April sittings in the station's weigh room; award 4 May.
Water (Vose), theft (Teague), hay (the 1908 report); 'no cause established'.
Four exhibits named, with the point that Strawn's 1923 notebook - carrying the condemnation entry - was in the room.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 with no finding; award 4 May 1925, $3,800, without admission, charged to the station account; the $3,500 pair rejected on the written award.
'a fifth of the $19,000 later computed', charged to the station account. The ironic identity with the gain account is not spelled out, but the item's own aspect - the account charged - is stated.
Ivy Keddie b.1931, Duncan's daughter and Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland; Vaught named with Bulletin 471.
'For the first time five records were put in one room' - all five listed.
February 1958, the loft ladder, the stenciled crate under a tarpaulin; nine pipettes, with the 'eleven' pair rejected on her measurement sheet.
9 March 1958, calibrated burette, nine readings listed, mean 16.72 against 17.6, short 0.88, '95 hundredths of the mark'.
1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923 low by one part in twenty; 3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80; the error stated as proportional.

All four: 40,000,000 lb over 25 full years 1898-1922, 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25 cents, and the ledger identity quoted from Bulletin 471 ('stands credited in the Association's own ledgers, year by year, as station gain').
Bulletin 471, October 1958, clearing him; thirty-five / thirty-three / twenty-four years stated explicitly.
Granddaughter.
Derivation via Duncan (b.1894) as Ansel's son and Ivy (b.1931) as Duncan's daughter; Chronicle and Falke's draft treated as one source and wrong.
Second cousins, with the full derivation through Emmet/Orra as siblings and Roy/Duncan as first cousins.

A08 abstention earned at its location: 'Left open: whether Emmet and Orra were full siblings', plus 'same degree' either way. The sheet asserts 'full sister' elsewhere - deduction applied separately per the collision rule.
Gideon Vose, his father; the nephew claim traced to Toland/Rundle and rejected on Vose's own words and Loomis's 'son of the late president'.
Significance: Gideon wrote Article VII, so the son managed under his father's rule and defended the office rather than suspect the instrument; the 4.56 Jerseys added.
A01 abstention: 'None that the sources establish'; the leaning sentence carries an attached declining qualifier ('the negative cannot be proven from these papers') and Section E marks it U.
What is established: two hearsay affirmations (Toland, Oram) against the best-placed witness's denial (Duncan); nothing written down.
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95; 95 percent of truth, one part in twenty; the 16.27 cascade rejected on Ivy's own readings.
3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80, short 0.19, given as 5 percent of 3.80.
76,000 x $0.25 = $19,000; patrons received $3,800 = 20 percent, one fifth.
360 x $0.24 = $86.40 with the 1910 price sourced to Brant's book; $90.00 given only as the period-average alternative.
Both denominators named - 5.26 percent of credited, 5.00 percent of delivered - and NT-20 rejected by name.
$77.93, with the five line items summed.
72 pipettes (six dozen), each short 17.6 - 16.72 = 0.88 c.c.
26 years 1 month 11 days (1 May 1897 - 12 June 1923) against 25 full delivery years 1898-1922, with the part-year reason stated.
A02 abstention: 'Cannot be determined', with the two memory figures and the missing ledger column.
Variable: the milk pipette, the station's own broken and a borrowed one substituted.
Constants: patrons, herds, pasture, season, acid, bottles, hand tester, the man and his habits, the scales, the book.
3.61 to 3.80 from 8 May, back to 3.61 on 10 July; 63 days, nine weeks; the 'six weeks' pair rejected.
Establishes the cause is the glass and not the milk, men or land; limits given (which measure was wrong needs the burette; magnitude not fixed; the interval is summer-only).
Five reasons, each attributed, drawn from Teague/Sill/Kyle, Keddie's book, Strawn, Ivy/Vaught and Frick.
Independence argued from different records in different hands; reasons 1, 2, 3 and 5 named as standing without the 1958 measurement.

A09 ASSERTED: 'Did Teague ever question his own entries? No.' and then, as fact, that he raised it with Vose in 1916 - r05's pole. Section E marks the same conflict U, but the item follows its location.
Answers the literal question yes, on the 1926 address and the 1919 circular.
Three of the five established points: manager from 1913 (Section E), signed the annual sheets, wrote the 1919 circular.
A03 ASSERTED: closes with an unqualified verdict - 'knew the tests were low, was told the gain existed, did not understand what it meant, and did not want to.'

Capped. Well over three ordinary conflicts found, resolved and methoded: six farms, nine families circularized, weigh book 1 Jan 1897, Orra born 1866, Selby manager 1913, Jan-Mar 1908 sampling, the crate in the loft, Ammon selling into Ordell in 1897, r07's swapped book attributions.
Capped. Twenty near-tie pairs listed with both carriers named and a breaker stated, including NT-1, NT-11, NT-14, NT-19 and NT-20.

A06 earned ('Not fully settled; U leaning Ivy', with r09's pole eliminated on Strawn's June visit) and A10 earned (U; by-laws undated, minutes lost in the 1938 move). A04 not earned: the sheet rejects the knowing-substitution pole outright ('I do not accept it') and treats the reground mold as probably the cause, never declaring the question unsettleable.
A dedicated self-refutation list - r03, r05, r06, r07, r11, r15, r18, r20. Buckets sum to 9; section capped at 8 per the key.

Cause, size, onset and cessation all derived: the 1897 Ammon lot at 16.72 against 17.6, the neck ruled for the full charge, 95 percent, 0.19 as 5 percent of 3.80, 1896 at 3.80 on borrowed glass, 1924 at 3.80 on new glass, nothing changing on the farms.
Watering named (Vose, echoed by Sill) and defeated by Strawn's lactometer from 1907, Cudd's vats, the constancy of the gap, the 1911 interval and the chronology.

Theft named (Teague at the hearing; Rundle, Toland, Oram's father) and defeated by the cream arriving heavy in the accuser's own ledger, the 1911 rise, and the 1923-24 rise with the same man at the bench.
Bog hay named (Grigg's 1908 committee, Kepp 1926, Falke's first draft) and defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths, the flat seasonal profile, Alder Corners, and the 1911 and 1923 shifts.
A07 ASSERTED: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.' - a headline verdict with no declining qualifier, followed by supporting argument.
A05 abstention: the verdict sentence is 'What the tester believed: not settled', and Section E marks it U; the later 'I weight Keddie's own papers and Duncan's memory' reads as a declared lean.
163 words against a 150-word cap.

At most three or four record series named (by-laws; the ledgers by implication of 'booked as station gain'; the arbitration; the 1958 measurement). 'Five books nobody had put in one room' names none of them; five required.
Clean: hay, water and theft attributed to the valley rather than asserted, and every headline figure right - 16.72, 17.6, 3.61, 3.80, $3,800, $19,000.
Arc complete at both ends: five percent short, 1897, $19,000, condemned in 1923 and unconnected, explained in 1958, both Keddies named.

deductions.reason: Corruption: asserts the Alder Corners cheese factory was 'built ... in 1913' as fact (planted error F055, r10), reconciling 1914 as the year it opened rather than rejecting 1913
Corruption: asserts Ansel Keddie 'went up in 1895 to ready it' (planted error F044 / NT-13, carried by r01 and r17); canon places him at the station only from 4 May 1896
Gullibility (A03): D3 settles what the manager knew - 'knew the tests were low, was told the gain existed, did not understand what it meant, and did not want to'
Gullibility (A07): Section F answers 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.'
Gullibility (A08): Story 6 states 'Orra was full sister to Emmet Brant' and Section E resolves it to full by I/M, although B2 correctly leaves it open
Gullibility (A09): D2 answers 'Did Teague ever question his own entries? No.' and asserts he raised it with Vose in 1916, although Section E marks the same conflict U
